The market generally expects Apple to launch a new OLED iPad mini by the end of this month. Today, an unconfirmed rumour once again claimed that the new iPad mini will switch to an OLED screen, but will still maintain a 60Hz refresh rate and will not support ProMotion.

The OLED version of the iPad mini may lack ProMotion

This is the second time we have heard this rumour, but both times it came from the same source: the yeux1122 account on Naver. That account has a very mixed track record on Apple rumours, often passing on information from anonymous sources verbatim rather than providing its own exclusive information.

However, yeux1122's latest post claims that overseas reports "mention the new OLED iPad mini will have 120Hz", but that "domestic production specifications have been confirmed" to use a 60Hz screen.

I must stress again that I have very strong doubts about this rumour, as no other reliable sources have corroborated it so far.

Nevertheless, if true, it would be a disappointing shortcoming for iPad mini buyers. This iPad mini upgrade is expected to bring a number of significant improvements, including:

  • OLED display.
  • Upgraded from the A17 Pro chip currently used in the iPad mini to the Apple A20 Pro chip.
  • A redesigned exterior with narrower bezels and possibly improved water resistance.
  • The FaceTime camera will move to the landscape edge, in line with Apple's other iPad models.

If Apple implements all of the above changes but fails to upgrade the display to a 120Hz ProMotion screen, it will inevitably take the shine off the new iPad mini's debut.

The new iPad mini is expected to be announced later this month, so we won't have to wait long to find out.

What do you think? Will the new iPad mini feature ProMotion with a 120Hz refresh rate? Let us know in the comments section.
